Digits up to n: n(n+1)/2 total terms.

Position 4501: find smallest n with n(n+1)/2 ≥ 4501. n=94: 94·95/2=4465. n=95: 4560. So 4501 is in the block of 95 (positions 4466–4560), digit 95 → the digit at that position is 95 repeated, as a number, so its digits are "9","5" per copy.

Careful: the sequence is digit-wise, so the number n is written out with its digits, repeated n times. So we need to count digits, not terms.

Count digits: numbers 1–9: each n repeated n times, 1 digit each: 45 digits.
Numbers 10–99: each n repeated n times, 2 digits each: sum of n from 10 to 99 = 4950−45 = 4905 copies, ×2 = 9810 digits. Total through 99 = 9855.

So the 4501st and 4052nd digits are within the two-digit range. After 9: 45 digits. Position 4501 → offset 4501−45 = 4456 digits into two-digit numbers. Position 4052 → offset 4007.

Digits through number m (from 10): 2·(m(m+1)/2 − 45) = m(m+1) − 90.

For offset 4456: need m(m+1) − 90 ≥ 4456 → m(m+1) ≥ 4546. m=67: 67·68=4556 ≥ 4546; m=66: 66·67=4422 <4546. So m=67. Digits through 66: 4422−90=4332. Offset 4456−4332=124 into block of 67 (134 digits). Position 124 is even → second digit of the copy: 7.

For offset 4007: m(m+1) ≥ 4097. m=63: 63·64=4032 <4097; m=64: 64·65=4160 ≥ 4097. Digits through 63: 4032−90=3942. Offset 4007−3942=65, odd → first digit of 64: 6.

Sum = 7+6 = 13.

ANSWER: 13
